data.name: Sherlock Holmes: The Mystery of the Mummy
data.detailed_description:
Destaque


Acerca do jogo

Inspirado n'As Aventuras de Sherlock Holmes Escrito por Sr Arthur Conan Doyle.
Após a morte de Lord Montcalfe, a sua filha Elisabeth vai ao encontro do famoso detetive Sherlock Holmes para resolver o mistério que rodeia a morte do seu pai. Como seu assistente confiável, Doutor Watson tem então umas merecidas férias com a sua família, Holmes decide ir para a mansão sozinho. Ele terá que usar toda a sua considerável habilidade para resolver todos os enigmas da mansão. Só então ele descobre que por detrás desse misterioso caso, se esconde um terrível segredo.
Em O Mistério da Múmia, vais estar imerso numa incrível aventura cheia de mistérios e com muitos desenvolvimentos. Assume o papel do famoso detetive Sherlock Holmes e prepara-te para evitar armadilhas e resolver inúmeros enigmas. Um misterioso assassino, numerosos suspeitos, e a famosa múmia para um caso que não parece ser assim tão fácil...

reviews.review:
Broken origins, broken code: a masterclass in frustration.

If you are thinking of picking up this franchise-starter on a modern PC, save your sanity and skip it. While the developer would eventually go on to make some incredible detective titles, their very first entry is a fundamentally broken, frustrating mess that holds up poorly in absolutely every department.

Here is why you should avoid this historical relic:

• Nightmarish modern incompatibility: Out of the box, the game is virtually unplayable on a modern machine. You will be greeted with broken screen sizes, an uncooperative or hyper-sensitive cursor, and constant crashes every time you try to transition to a new level. To even get it running, you are forced to hunt down external third-party software like DxWnd, tweak profile settings, and run backend applications in the background just to navigate the main menu.

• Obnoxious pixel-hunting and moon logic: The puzzle design is aggressively anti-intuitive. Instead of utilizing clever deduction or observation, the gameplay drops you into a first-person perspective where you will spend hours pixel-hunting for tiny, blurry items hidden in grainy environments. Miss a single obscure object—like a near-impossible-to-see hairpin—and your progress is completely soft-locked until you look up an external guide.

• Grating audio and painful presentation: The technical presentation is completely agonizing. The sound design features ears-piercing, repetitive background tracks that abruptly cut off and restart, mixed alongside clipping audio. To make matters worse, the main character is saddled with an incredibly irritating nasal voice delivery that spouts obvious, silly remarks instead of actual brilliant insights.

• Massive narrative disconnect: For a detective game, it barely feels like a mystery story at all. Outside of the opening and closing cutscenes, the narrative completely vanishes. The entire middle of the game is just a series of survival-horror-style room escape traps that have zero bearing on the actual plot, plagued by clunky writing and bad grammar.

Final Verdict: Even when given away for free, this game demands too much troubleshooting and offers far too little enjoyment in return. It is an outdated chore that belongs in the past. Do yourself a favor, skip this broken origin story, and jump straight into the developer's vastly superior modern sequels instead.
